full_judgment:
4. Plaint case, in short, is that the land measuring about 0.6864 acre of plot No. 118 appertaining to CS khatian No. 13369 was originally owned and possessed by Indro Mohan and Rajkumar and Mukta Sundari in equal shares. Indro Mohan and Mukta Sundari died without any issue and leaving Rajkumar as their only heir and legal representative. Rajkumar was survived by two sons, namely, Radhagobinda and Pratap Chandra. By successive devolution, Radhagobinda and others became owners in possession of said land. They on 2-1-54 transferred said land to the plaintiff by way of a registered 'Patta' being No. 7441 and a registered sale deed being No. 7442 and delivered possession. Record of rights was accordingly prepared in the names of said recorded tenants and the plaintiff in SA khatian No. 2190 in plot No. 6163. Said land was also recorded as holding No. 47 Lal Chan Mokim Lane in the office of defendant No. 4, the DCC. 

 12. It was further stated that the plaintiff got recorded 0.3292 acre in his name in the DP Khatian No. 5392 behind the back of the DCC. Against said record of rights, an appeal was filed and decided wrongly against the DCC. Then, an application was made for review which was fixed for hearing on 25-6-03. Against the review order, the petitioner moved this Division and got a stay in Writ Petition No. 4522 of 2003. By transfer from the DIT the DCC became owner of the suit land. The plaintiff has got no right or title in the suit land and the suit was therefore not maintainable. 

 17. On appeal therefrom at the instance of the plaintiff, the appellate Court on the other hand on the evidence both oral and documentary on record found 0.2435 acre of land was finally released and the plaintiff returned the money as was required for such release of the unused land. It found possession of the plaintiff in the suit land which was admitted by defendant No. 4. It also found RS Khatian was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.5. 

 34. Further case of the plaintiff was that the land of schedule 'Kha' measuring 0.3480 was recorded wrongly in the name of DIT in the revision survey in RS khatian No.6, which had no basis. In support of such case, he adduced evidence both oral and documentary. 

 36. It was also the view of the trial Court that RS khatian might have been prepared in 1969/70 to 1972/73 and the plaintiff got release of the land in 1986. So, there was no occasion for recording the land in the name of the plaintiff. Such record of rights cast a doubt over the title of plaintiff and the declaration sought for in respect of the wrong record of rights was not sufficient in the absence of a declaration of title. 

 49. The Court of appeal below decreed the suit that the record of rights as prepared in Khatian No. 06 in respect of 0.3480 acre of schedule 'Kha' in the name of DIT (RAJUK) was illegal, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff as prayed for. I find such declaration was not sufficient, effective and complete relief. Because, the record of rights would not be corrected even after such declaration and continue to remain as before, with at best a copy of the decree attached with the relevant page. 

 58. The suit is accordingly decreed declaring the record of rights as prepared and finally published vide Exhibit 11/Ka in respect of land measuring about 3480 described in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint in the name of the then DIT and now RAJUK in RS Khatian No. 6 is wrong, illegal, ineffective and not binding upon the plaintiff. It is directed that the relevant record of rights must be corrected in the name of the plaintiff.
